title: Past continuous + question words 2 + this / that
title_it: Past continuous + parole interrogative 2 + this / that
goal: Say what was happening at a moment in the past, ask how much, how many, how far, how long and how often, and use this, these, that and those.
goal_it: Dire cosa stava succedendo in un momento del passato, fare domande con how much, how many, how far, how long e how often, e usare this, these, that e those.

steps.title: Past continuous: actions in progress
en: We use the past continuous (was / were + verb-ing) for an action that was in progress at a moment in the past. It had started before that moment and was not finished.
Example: at 10.30 yesterday they were playing tennis. We do not say when they started or finished; we only say what was happening at 10.30.
It is often the background of a story: It was raining and people were running for the bus.
it: Usiamo il past continuous (was / were + verbo-ing) per un'azione in corso a un momento del passato. Era cominciata prima di quel momento e non era finita.
Esempio: ieri alle 10.30 stavano giocando a tennis. Non diciamo quando hanno iniziato o finito; diciamo solo cosa stava succedendo alle 10.30.
Spesso è lo sfondo di una storia: It was raining and people were running for the bus (Pioveva e la gente correva per prendere l'autobus).

examples.en: At eight o'clock last night I was cooking dinner.
examples.it: Ieri sera alle otto stavo preparando la cena.

examples.en: They were sitting on the sofa in the living room.
examples.it: Erano seduti sul divano in soggiorno.

examples.en: What were you doing at nine?

steps.title: Past continuous: negative, questions and special cases
steps.title_it: Past continuous: negativa, domanda e casi particolari
en: Negative: wasn't / weren't + verb-ing (It wasn't raining). Question: Was / Were + subject + verb-ing? (Were you sleeping?). Short answers: Yes, I was. / No, we weren't.
Remember the difference with the past simple. Past continuous: the action was in progress (We were walking home when I met Dan). Past simple: the action is complete, or short and sudden (I met Dan).

When and while: we use while with the longer action (while we were having dinner) and when with the short action that interrupts (when the phone rang). While is not a question word: it joins two parts of a sentence.
Verbs of state (know, want, like, understand, have = possess) are not normally used in the continuous: I knew the answer, not I was knowing.
it: Negativa: wasn't / weren't + verbo-ing (It wasn't raining). Domanda: Was / Were + soggetto + verbo-ing? (Were you sleeping?). Risposte brevi: Yes, I was. / No, we weren't.
Attenzione alla differenza con il past simple. Past continuous: l'azione era in corso (We were walking home when I met Dan). Past simple: l'azione è completa, oppure breve e improvvisa (I met Dan).

When e while: while va con l'azione più lunga (while we were having dinner), when con l'azione breve che interrompe (when the phone rang). While non è una parola interrogativa: collega due parti di una frase.
I verbi di stato (know, want, like, understand, have = possedere) di solito non si usano alla forma continua: I knew the answer, non I was knowing.

examples.en: Matt phoned while we were having dinner.
It was raining when I got up.
I was having a shower when the doorbell rang.
examples.it: Stavo facendo la doccia quando ha suonato il campanello.

steps.title: Question words 2: how much, how many, how far, how long, how often
steps.title_it: Parole interrogative 2: how much, how many, how far, how long, how often
en: How much + uncountable noun: How much milk do we need? How many + countable plural noun: How many people came?
How far asks about distance: How far is the station? How long asks about time: How long did the film last? Never say how long time. How often asks about frequency: How often do you go to the gym?
The order is the same as in all questions: question word + auxiliary + subject + verb. Use the tense that the time clue asks for (yesterday = past simple, now = present continuous).
it: How much + nome uncountable: How much milk do we need? How many + nome countable al plurale: How many people came?
How far chiede la distanza: How far is the station? How long chiede il tempo: How long did the film last? Mai how long time. How often chiede la frequenza: How often do you go to the gym?
L'ordine è lo stesso di tutte le domande: parola interrogativa + ausiliare + soggetto + verbo. Usa il tempo che chiede l'indizio (yesterday = past simple, now = present continuous).

examples.en: How much money did you spend?
How many rooms are there in the hotel?
How far is it from the flat to the bus stop?
examples.it: Quanto è lontano dall'appartamento alla fermata dell'autobus?

examples.en: How long have we got? How often do you cook?
examples.it: Quanto tempo abbiamo? Ogni quanto cucini?

steps.title: This, these, that, those
en: This / these = near me (in space or time). That / those = far from me. This and that go with singular nouns; these and those go with plural nouns.
On the phone and when we introduce people we use this: Hello, this is Anna. Is that Tom?
it: This / these = vicino a me (nello spazio o nel tempo). That / those = lontano da me. This e that con il singolare; these e those con il plurale.
Al telefono e quando presentiamo qualcuno si usa this: Hello, this is Anna. Is that Tom?

examples.en: This is my pen, here in my hand.
examples.it: Questa è la mia penna, qui nella mia mano.

examples.en: That picture on the wall is beautiful.
examples.it: Quel quadro sul muro è bellissimo.

examples.en: Look at those clouds over there.

steps.q: At eight o'clock last night I ___ dinner.
steps.q_it: Ieri sera alle otto stavo preparando la cena.
steps.why: A moment in the past (eight o'clock) and an action in progress: past continuous.
steps.why_it: Un momento nel passato (le otto) e un'azione in corso: past continuous.

steps.q: At 10.30 yesterday morning they ___ (play) tennis.
steps.q_it: Ieri mattina alle 10.30 stavano giocando a tennis.
steps.why: They is plural, so were + playing.
steps.why_it: They è plurale, quindi were + playing.

steps.q: A: What ___ (you / do) at nine last night? B: I was watching TV.
steps.q_it: A: Cosa stavi facendo ieri sera alle nove? B: Guardavo la TV.
steps.why: Question: were + subject + verb-ing.
steps.why_it: Domanda: were + soggetto + verbo-ing.

steps.q: It ___ (not / rain) when we left the house.
steps.q_it: Non pioveva quando siamo usciti di casa.
steps.why: Negative past continuous: wasn't + verb-ing.
steps.why_it: Negativa del past continuous: wasn't + verbo-ing.

steps.q: ___ the children sleeping when you got home? No, they were playing.
steps.q_it: I bambini dormivano quando sei arrivato a casa? No, giocavano.
steps.why: Question with the children (they): Were + subject + verb-ing.
steps.why_it: Domanda con the children (they): Were + soggetto + verbo-ing.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine.
answers: She was reading a book on the train
steps.why: Subject + was + verb-ing, then the place.
steps.why_it: Soggetto + was + verbo-ing, poi il luogo.

steps.q: Which sentence is correct?
steps.q_it: Quale frase è corretta?
steps.why: Know is a verb of state, so we use the simple form: knew.
steps.why_it: Know è un verbo di stato, quindi si usa la forma semplice: knew.

steps.q: I ___ my keys while I was running for the bus.
steps.q_it: Ho perso le chiavi mentre correvo per prendere l'autobus.
steps.why: Losing the keys is a short, complete action inside a longer one: past simple. The longer action (was running) is in the past continuous.
steps.why_it: Perdere le chiavi è un'azione breve e completa dentro una più lunga: past simple. L'azione più lunga (was running) è al past continuous.

steps.q: It was raining when I ___ (get) up.
steps.q_it: Pioveva quando mi sono alzato.
steps.why: Getting up is a short action that happened at that time: past simple (got).
steps.why_it: Alzarsi è un'azione breve avvenuta in quel momento: past simple (got).

steps.q: Matt phoned while we ___ (have) dinner.
steps.q_it: Matt ha telefonato mentre cenavamo.
steps.why: While introduces the longer action in progress: past continuous.
steps.why_it: While introduce l'azione più lunga in corso: past continuous.

steps.q: I was having a shower ___ the doorbell rang.
steps.q_it: Stavo facendo la doccia quando ha suonato il campanello.
steps.why: When goes with the short action that interrupts (rang). While would go with a longer action.
steps.why_it: When va con l'azione breve che interrompe (rang). While andrebbe con un'azione più lunga.

steps.q: We were walking home when we ___ (meet) Dan.
steps.q_it: Stavamo tornando a casa a piedi quando abbiamo incontrato Dan.
steps.why: The meeting is short and complete: past simple (met).
steps.why_it: L'incontro è breve e completo: past simple (met).

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine.
answers: They were having lunch when it started to rain
steps.why: Longer action (were having) first, then when + short action in the past simple.
steps.why_it: Prima l'azione lunga (were having), poi when + azione breve al past simple.

steps.q: ___ milk do we need for the cake?
steps.q_it: Quanto latte ci serve per la torta?
steps.why: Milk is uncountable, so we use how much.
steps.why_it: Milk è uncountable, quindi si usa how much.

steps.q: ___ people came to the party on Saturday?
steps.q_it: Quante persone sono venute alla festa sabato?
steps.why: People is a countable plural noun: how many.
steps.why_it: People è un nome countable plurale: how many.

steps.q: ___ is it from here to the station? About two kilometres.
steps.q_it: Quanto è lontana la stazione da qui? Circa due chilometri.
steps.why: Distance: how far.
steps.why_it: Distanza: how far.

steps.q: How ___ did the film last? Two hours.
steps.q_it: Quanto è durato il film? Due ore.
steps.why: Duration: how long. We never say how long time.
steps.why_it: Durata: how long. Non si dice mai how long time.

steps.q: Make a question.
steps.q_it: Forma una domanda.
answers: How often do you go to the gym
steps.why: How often + do + subject + base verb.
steps.why_it: How often + do + soggetto + verbo base.

steps.q: Look at ___ birds in the tree over there.
steps.q_it: Guarda quegli uccelli sull'albero laggiù.
steps.why: Birds is plural and far from us: those.
steps.why_it: Birds è plurale e lontano da noi: those.

steps.q: (holding a phone) ___ is my new phone.
steps.q_it: (tenendo in mano un telefono) Questo è il mio telefono nuovo.
steps.why: Singular and near me: this.
steps.why_it: Singolare e vicino a me: this.

steps.q: Look at ___ shoes I'm wearing. I bought them yesterday.
steps.q_it: Guarda queste scarpe che indosso. Le ho comprate ieri.
steps.why: Shoes is plural and on my feet, so near: these.
steps.why_it: Shoes è plurale ed è ai miei piedi, quindi vicino: these.

steps.q: A: What were you doing when I called? B: I ___ a shower.
steps.q_it: A: Cosa facevi quando ho chiamato? B: Facevo la doccia.
steps.why: The answer to 'What were you doing?' is an action in progress: past continuous.
steps.why_it: La risposta a 'What were you doing?' è un'azione in corso: past continuous.

steps.q: How many eggs ___ you buy yesterday?
steps.q_it: Quante uova hai comprato ieri?
steps.why: Yesterday is a finished time, so past simple: did + you + buy.
steps.why_it: Yesterday è un tempo finito, quindi past simple: did + you + buy.

steps.q: Yesterday I ___ (not / see) Anna.
steps.q_it: Ieri non ho visto Anna.
steps.why: Past simple negative: didn't + base verb.
steps.why_it: Negativa del past simple: didn't + verbo base.

steps.q: The keys are ___ the table, next to the lamp.
steps.q_it: Le chiavi sono sul tavolo, accanto alla lampada.
steps.why: On = on a surface, touching it.
steps.why_it: On = su una superficie, a contatto.

steps.q: ___ did you go on holiday? In August.
steps.q_it: Quando sei andato in vacanza? Ad agosto.
steps.why: The answer is a time (in August): when.
steps.why_it: La risposta è un tempo (in August): when.

cards.ex: She was reading on the train.
I was cooking while he was studying.
I was walking when it started to rain.
How much money did you spend?
How many chairs are there in the room?
How long did the lesson last?
These shoes are on the floor.
That picture is on the wall.
